collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 30 or older)

collection.description: A villager passes the wrong turn that led to a lifelong friend: take it again, or go and tell the friend.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Years ago, (name1) got lost on the way to the far gardens, took the wrong path and ended up at the stream, where (he/she) sat down, annoyed, next to someone (he/she) had never really talked to before. They're still friends. Today, walking the same path, (name1) passes that exact wrong turn and stops.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) takes it, just for old times' sake. It still leads to the stream. There's nobody sitting there today. (name1) sits down anyway. It's a lovely spot. (He/she) thinks about how much of (his/her) life came from that one mistake: the friendship, and then all the people that friend introduced (him/her) to, and everything after. (He/she) laughs. (He/she) has been grateful to a wrong turn for years without noticing.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (name1) goes to find the friend and reminds them about that day. The friend doesn't remember it at all. "You sat next to me? At the stream?" "You were eating a mango. Very messily." "...That does sound like me." They laugh. (name1) realizes the most important day of (his/her) life is one the other person can't even remember. (He/she) finds this very funny.
